key_results: Curvature principally changes equatorial ligament behavior rather than centerline compression.
The final fixed-point/K-H angle shifts with curvature radius while shock intensity mainly changes the critical contact angle.

mechanisms.summary: Curvature redistributes surface-normal and tangential loading; coupled internal/external waves establish the fixed point where K-H develops.

evidence_candidates.claim: For the modeled divergent shock, curvature shifts ligament formation upstream and sustains greater spanwise extension relative to the planar comparison.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Full-field comparisons resolve altered normal and tangential loading and associated ligament morphology.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Two-dimensional cylindrical droplet; viscosity, capillarity and phase transition omitted.

evidence_candidates.claim: The windward K-H inception site nearly coincides with a migrating fixed point created by combined external and internal wave loading.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Table 1 and the theoretical construction connect the critical transmitted-shock contact point to the final fixed point and K-H onset.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Mechanism is developed for the simplified two-dimensional configuration.
